About The Role

As the Program Manager, Employee Experience, you are the creative producer, event architect, and visual activation engine behind our company culture and employee engagement. In this role, you will bridge corporate, retail, and operational teams to foster an informed, connected, and inspired workforce.

You will partner cross-functionally with leaders, People Team members, and subject matter experts across the business to gather raw ideas, refine and polish messaging, and package it into compelling, accessible formats. You will take full ownership of our flagship company-wide newsletter, end-to-end event execution (Town Halls, All-Hands, cultural milestones), on-brand graphic design activations, channel governance, and LinkedIn employer branding amplification. This is a high-visibility, hands-on role ideal for a proactive producer who thrives in a collaborative, evolving environment.

What You Get To Do Every Day

Event Production & Cultural Programming: Own the end-to-end creative concept, run-of-show logistics, slide deck formatting, speaker prep, and live technical execution for company-wide meetings (All-Hands, Town Halls, Fireside Chats). Conceptualize and produce interactive cultural moments, employee appreciation weeks, and ERG milestones.
Company-Wide Newsletter & Content Packaging: Own the end-to-end layout, visual design, and distribution of our recurring company-wide newsletter. Partner with department leads and project owners across the business to source updates, refine raw content for tone and clarity, and package it into engaging, scannable digests.
Graphic Activations & Visual Assets: Design on-brand presentation decks, digital signage, Slack banners, visual toolkits, infographics, and bite-sized multimedia assets (GIFs, short video recaps using Descript/Canva) to make company-wide updates visually compelling and digestible.
Collaborative Content Refining & Storytelling: Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to help refine, edit, and optimize announcements and talking points, ensuring communications are clear and aligned with company voice.
Employer Brand, LinkedIn & Glassdoor Amplification: Collaborate with Talent Acquisition and Marketing to translate internal wins, culture spotlights, and employee milestones into engaging LinkedIn posts and employer profile updates (e.g., LinkedIn Life pages, Glassdoor employer branding) that elevate our reputation and strengthen talent attraction.
Channel Governance & Measurement: Partner with business leads to govern Slack channels and internal hubs, reducing information noise across corporate and frontline teams while tracking readership and event engagement metrics.

What You Bring To The Role

4–6+ years of experience in employee experience, internal communications, corporate events, or employer branding, with a proven track record of creating compelling programming and tailored content for diverse, multi-segmented workforces—including hourly, corporate, remote, retail, and field/operational populations.
Proven track record managing end-to-end corporate events (All-Hands, panel discussions, hybrid broadcasts) with senior executives.
Exceptional writing, editing, and storytelling skills; ability to distill complex initiatives into concise, relatable copy.

Strong emotional intelligence and confidence working directly with executive leaders and cross-functional teams.

Experience supporting diverse workforces (e.g., hybrid, corporate, retail, or remote environments).
Familiarity with workplace communication tools (e.g., Slack).
Basic video editing capabilities (e.g., Canva, CapCut) for internal recap reels.

new_jobs.title: Technical Program Manager (TPM)
new_jobs.description:
Overview

LMI is seeking a Senior Technical Program Manager (TPM) to lead the delivery of LMI's technology portfolio supporting the United States Postal Service (USPS). USPS operates the nation's largest delivery and logistics network and is in the midst of a multi-year modernization effort to improve service reliability, transform the customer experience, and achieve long-term financial sustainability. The TPM will be LMI's senior technical leader on this account: owning the end-to-end deployment of technology solutions into the USPS environment and serving as the trusted advisor who connects hands-on engineering execution to USPS mission and business outcomes.

This is a hands-on leadership role for a professional who can lead the deployment of a diverse portfolio of enterprise technologies into a large, complex federal environment, including ServiceNow, the Microsoft ecosystem (Microsoft 365, Power Platform, Azure), AI-enabled and agentic solutions, custom software applications, AI-assisted software engineering approaches, and commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) products. The TPM manages a portfolio of concurrent technology projects and deployments, sets and enforces best practices across software development, customer/user experience (CX/UX) design, security, and release management, and is personally accountable for the cost, schedule, quality, and adoption of every solution the team delivers. Equally important to the technical mandate is customer management and relationship building. The TPM builds and sustains strong working relationships with USPS stakeholders, translating their needs into actionable solution roadmaps, communicating clearly across both technical and non-technical audiences, driving consensus, and continuously demonstrating value. The role demands someone who thrives in an environment that emphasizes building, deploying, and iterating in parallel, and who can own the full solution lifecycle alongside the client.

Role Scope & Authority

This senior leadership role reports to the LMI USPS Account Lead and serves as LMI’s primary technical leader on the account. The position oversees a portfolio of multiple concurrent technology initiatives and leads a multidisciplinary team of engineers, architects, designers, analysts, and subcontractors.

The TPM has broad authority to set delivery standards, prioritize and sequence work, approve technical approaches, escalate risks to USPS and LMI leadership, and recommend staffing and resource decisions. The role interacts regularly with USPS senior IT and business stakeholders at the director and executive levels.

About LMI

LMI is a new breed of digital solutions provider dedicated to accelerating government impact with innovation and speed. Investing in technology and prototypes ahead of need, LMI brings commercial-grade platforms and mission-ready AI to federal agencies at commercial speed.

Leveraging our mission-ready technology and solutions, proven expertise in federal deployment, and strategic relationships, we enhance outcomes for the government, efficiently and effectively. With a focus on agility and collaboration, LMI serves the defense, space, healthcare, and energy sectors—helping agencies navigate complexity and outpace change. Headquartered in Tysons, Virginia, LMI is committed to delivering impactful results that strengthen missions and drive lasting value.

Responsibilities

Portfolio Delivery & Execution:
Serve as LMI's senior technical lead and primary technical point of contact for the USPS account.
On-time, on-budget delivery of technology solutions into the USPS production environment across multiple platforms and technologies.
Build and sustain trusted relationships with USPS stakeholders, acting as the senior advisor on solution approach and continuously identifying opportunities to add value and expand impact.
Own the end-to-end lifecycle of technology deployments into the USPS environment (e.g., intake, solution design, build, integration, test, deployment, and sustainment)
Prioritize, sequence, balance workload, and allocate resources to effectively manage and deconflict a portfolio of concurrent technology projects and deployments

Technical Leadership & Standards:
Translate USPS mission and business needs into technical solution architectures, delivery roadmaps, and Agile backlogs that integrate cleanly with existing USPS systems, data, and enterprise IT.
Lead delivery using Agile methodologies (Scrum, SAFe, and/or Kanban): manage the backlog, sprints, and release planning; run ceremonies; and drive CI/CD and DevSecOps practices for fast, reliable, and secure delivery.
Apply human-centered design and CX/UX best practices throughout delivery so solutions are usable, accessible, and adopted, not just deployed.
Direct the configuration and deployment of platform solutions, as well as bespoke and AI-assisted custom development where a tailored build is the right answer.
Stay current on emerging technology, to include GenAI and agentic AI, low-code/no-code platforms, cloud and platform advances, and modern development tooling, and bring practical innovation to the account.

Quality & Portfolio Management:
Govern technical quality and enforce architecture, coding, integration, and release standards across the team and partner contractors.
Manage cost, schedule, scope, and performance across the portfolio; track financials, forecast spend, prevent cost overruns, and report status against budget and milestones.
Proactively identify and mitigate technical, security, schedule, and delivery risks, implementing corrective actions before they impact the client.
Ensure compliance with USPS and federal cybersecurity, authorization/ATO, data governance, AI risk-management, privacy, and accessibility (Section 508) requirements.
Build, lead, and grow a multidisciplinary team (engineers, architects, designers, data and analytics specialists, and analysts); manage staffing, onboarding, task assignment, performance, and subcontractor coordination.
Develop and maintain technical and program documentation, including solution and system architectures, integration/interface designs, agent and workflow specifications, runbooks, and standard operating procedures.
Provide clear, regular status updates, briefings, and after-action reviews to USPS leadership and LMI management; record decisions and action items and keep stakeholders aligned.
Manage contract deliverables, milestones, schedules, and service levels, ensuring high-quality, on-time submissions and adherence to contractual and governance requirements.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

Education: Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information technology, software engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent professional experience.
Experience: Minimum of 10 years of experience spanning software engineering, solution architecture, and/or technical program/project management, including enterprise technology delivery and cloud deployments.
Technical & Delivery Expertise:
Demonstrated experience owning end-to-end deployments of enterprise technology into production across two or more of: the Microsoft ecosystem (Microsoft 365 / Power Platform / Azure), AI/GenAI solutions, COTS products, and custom software development.
Experience working the architecture of ServiceNow
Deep, working knowledge of modern software development practices, including DevSecOps and CI/CD.
Proven experience leading Agile delivery (Scrum, SAFe, and/or Kanban), including managing Agile teams, backlogs, and release cadences.
Demonstrated experience managing a portfolio of concurrent projects, with direct accountability for cost, schedule, scope, quality, and risk.
Working familiarity with federal IT governance, cybersecurity, authorization/ATO, data governance, and accessibility (Section 508) requirements.
Experience delivering technology in a federal government or comparably large, complex enterprise environment.

Program & Portfolio Management Expertise:
Strong stakeholder-management and customer-relationship skills, including the ability to brief and align senior/executive, non-technical leaders and to drive consensus.
Ability to clearly communicate complex technical concepts to non-technical audiences, both verbally and in writing.
Strong proficiency with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) for documentation, analysis, and executive briefings.

Certifications: Project Management Professional (PMP) or equivalent demonstrated program-management credential, and a recognized Agile/Scrum certification (e.g., PMI-ACP, Certified ScrumMaster (CSM), Professional Scrum Master (PSM), or SAFe).
Clearance / Eligibility: U.S. citizenship and the ability to obtain and maintain a USPS Public Trust Clearance

Preferred Qualifications

Education: Master's degree or better in computer science, engineering, or a related technical field, or an MBA with a technology focus.
Experience: Prior USPS or postal experience, or experience supporting other federal civilian agencies, specifically with technology deployments or the management of a portfolio of technology solutions.
Technical & Delivery Expertise:
Hands-on experience with GenAI and agentic AI platforms and AI-assisted/agentic development tooling (e.g., AI coding assistants and agent frameworks), including rapid AI-assisted (“vibe”) development.
Human-centered design, CX, or UX credentials, or a demonstrated portfolio of user-centered solution delivery.
Experience obtaining an Authority to Operate (ATO) / authorization for a SaaS or PaaS solution.
Experience with low-code/no-code platforms.
High-level technical understanding of data engineering, ETL, data analytics, and machine learning.

Program & Portfolio Management Expertise:
Experience leading distributed, multidisciplinary teams and managing subcontractors on federal contracts.

Certifications:
ServiceNow certifications (e.g., Certified System Administrator (CSA), Certified Implementation Specialist (CIS), Certified Application Developer (CAD)).
Microsoft certifications (e.g., Azure, Power Platform, or Microsoft 365).
Cloud certifications (AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud).
Advanced Agile / scaled-Agile certifications (e.g., SAFe Program Consultant (SPC) or Release Train Engineer (RTE)).
IT service management credentials (e.g., ITIL).
Cybersecurity certifications (e.g., CompTIA Security+, CISSP, or CISM).

new_jobs.description:
Summary

We are seeking an experienced Microsoft-focussed Delivery Lead
to lead system integration projects from mobilisation through completion. The role is accountable for client outcomes, delivery performance, commercial control and stakeholder confidence across projects involving multidisciplinary, distributed and third-party teams.

The ideal candidate is a consulting-focused delivery professional with strong general project and program delivery skills. They will combine structured governance with practical leadership, sound commercial judgement and the ability to manage scope, contracts, financials, risk, quality and client expectations. Experience delivering Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM or ERP solutions is desirable but not essential.

Key Responsibilities

End-to-End Delivery Leadership

Own delivery outcomes across scope, schedule, budget, quality, risk, dependencies and benefits.
Mobilise engagements by translating contractual commitments into an integrated delivery plan, governance model, resource plan and delivery controls.
Establish clear roles, decision rights, escalation paths, milestones, acceptance criteria and reporting expectations.
Lead Agile, Hybrid or Waterfall delivery approaches appropriate to the engagement.
Maintain an integrated view of workstreams, critical path, dependencies, client obligations and delivery readiness.
Drive timely decisions, resolve delivery blockers and intervene early when performance varies from plan.
Lead delivery through discovery, design, build, test, deployment, transition and closure, as applicable.
Ensure lessons learned, handover activities and closure obligations are completed.

Project Management

Build trusted client relationships and act as the principal delivery contact for senior stakeholders.
Facilitate discovery workshops, governance forums, steering committees, planning sessions and executive reviews.
Translate business objectives and consulting recommendations into achievable delivery outcomes.
Provide clear, evidence-based advice on priorities, trade-offs, delivery options and impacts.
Challenge assumptions constructively and help clients make informed decisions.
Align business, functional and technical stakeholders around scope, outcomes and delivery priorities.
Communicate complex delivery matters clearly to executive and non-technical audiences.
Identify opportunities to improve client outcomes, extend value or support follow-on work without compromising current delivery commitments.
Manage difficult conversations professionally, including delays, scope pressure, quality concerns and unmet client obligations.

Contract Management

Review and understand the contract, Statement of Work, assumptions, exclusions, dependencies, deliverables, acceptance criteria and client obligations.
Translate contractual commitments into delivery controls, work plans and traceable acceptance arrangements.
Maintain alignment between contracted scope, the delivery backlog, solution design, schedule, resourcing and financial forecasts.
Monitor client and supplier obligations and address late, incomplete or changed inputs before they affect delivery.
Identify scope gaps, ambiguity, relief events and contractual risks early and escalate them appropriately.
Lead change control by assessing impacts to scope, schedule, cost, resources, quality and benefits.
Prepare change requests and support commercial negotiations with account, legal and commercial stakeholders.
Prevent uncontrolled scope growth and ensure additional effort is formally assessed and approved before commitment.
Manage deliverable submission, review, acceptance, rejection and remediation in accordance with the contract.
Maintain appropriate documentation and evidence to support contractual and commercial decisions.

Commercial Management

Own project budgets, forecasts, revenue, cost, margin and financial performance.
Monitor sold-versus-delivered performance, burn rate, effort, resource utilisation and estimate-to-complete.
Reconcile the delivery plan, staffing model and financial forecast regularly.
Identify margin erosion, unplanned effort or forecast variance early and implement corrective action.
Validate time, expenses, milestones and invoicing inputs.
Work with account and commercial leaders to manage contractual exposure, change requests and recovery plans.
Balance customer outcomes with responsible commercial decision-making.
Contribute to proposals, estimates, delivery models, Statements of Work and pre-sales reviews.
Support delivery readiness and solution-to-delivery handover before commitments are made to clients.

Governance

Establish fit-for-purpose governance that supports timely decisions rather than administrative reporting.
Maintain and actively manage risks, issues, assumptions, dependencies, decisions and actions.
Produce concise status reporting focused on outcomes, variance, decisions, customer impact and required intervention.
Escalate bad news early, with clear facts, impacts, options and recommendations.
Define quality gates, review points and acceptance evidence across the lifecycle.
Ensure deliverables meet contractual requirements, agreed acceptance criteria and professional quality standards.
Coordinate independent assurance or quality reviews where required and drive resulting corrective actions.
Maintain delivery compliance with organisational methods, policies, security requirements and client governance.
Protect delivery evidence, approvals and decision records.

Stakeholder Management

Act as the primary delivery interface for client sponsors, executives and governance forums.
Set and manage realistic expectations regarding scope, timing, cost, quality and client dependencies.
Build alignment across client, account, practice, vendor and delivery stakeholders.
Prepare and lead steering committee discussions, presenting a clear view of status, decisions, risks and recovery actions.
Tailor communications to executive, business, functional and technical audiences.
Maintain stakeholder confidence through transparency, consistency and follow-through.
Manage escalations calmly and coordinate an agreed response across the engagement leadership team.

Team and Resource Leadership

Lead cross-functional teams including architects, consultants, developers, engineers, business analysts, testers, change specialists and project support.
Coordinate onshore, offshore, nearshore, client and third-party contributors.
Establish team ways of working, delivery rhythms, accountability and collaboration expectations.
Manage resource demand, capacity, onboarding, performance and role clarity.
Create an inclusive environment where risks and concerns can be raised early.
Coach workstream leads and project team members in delivery disciplines and client engagement.
Hold individuals and teams accountable for commitments while supporting resolution of impediments.
Promote continuous improvement, reusable assets and efficient delivery practices.

Business Applications Delivery

The Delivery Lead may lead engagements involving enterprise business applications, integration, data, cloud, security, workplace or digital transformation solutions.

Experience With The Following Is Desirable

Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Engagement / CRM.
Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations / ERP.
Power Platform, Dataverse and Power BI.
Business process transformation, fit-gap analysis and requirements traceability.
Data migration, integration, testing, deployment, cutover and hypercare.
Azure DevOps or comparable backlog and work-management tooling.
Multi-vendor or systems-integration programs.

The Delivery Lead is not expected to be the solution architect but must be able to understand delivery implications, challenge plans and facilitate informed decisions with functional and technical leaders.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications and Experience

Significant experience leading enterprise consulting, technology or business transformation engagements.
Demonstrated accountability for project scope, schedule, budget, risk, quality and client outcomes.
Strong understanding of consulting delivery, governance and professional services environments.
Experience managing contracts, Statements of Work, deliverables, assumptions, client obligations and change control.
Strong commercial and financial management capability, including forecasting, margin management and estimate-to-complete.
Experience leading multidisciplinary and distributed teams.
Strong stakeholder management, facilitation, negotiation and executive communication skills.
Demonstrated ability to manage ambiguity, resolve conflict and recover challenged delivery.
Working knowledge of Agile, Hybrid and Waterfall delivery approaches.
Experience with enterprise project planning, RAID management, resource management and governance reporting.
Strong written communication and the ability to produce clear executive-level materials.

Desirable Experience

Delivery experience across Microsoft technology or enterprise business applications.
Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM / Customer Engagement implementation experience.
Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations / ERP implementation experience.
Experience delivering Power Platform, data, integration or cloud-enabled transformation.
Experience working for a consulting organisation, systems integrator or Microsoft partner.
Experience with complex fixed-price, time-and-materials or outcome-based engagements.
Experience supporting proposals, estimates, solution reviews and pre-sales activities.
Experience managing third-party vendors, offshore teams or multi-partner delivery models.

Preferred Certifications

Delivery and Project Management

PMP.
PRINCE2 Practitioner.
Certified ScrumMaster or equivalent Agile certification.
PMI-ACP or equivalent.
ITIL Foundation or higher.
Relevant delivery leadership or professional services certification.

Microsoft

Microsoft certifications are desirable rather than mandatory and may include:

Dynamics 365 Fundamentals (CRM).
Dynamics 365 Fundamentals (ERP).
Power Platform Fundamentals.
Azure Fundamentals.
Other role-relevant Microsoft certifications.

Job Title:
Technical Project Manager, Energy Storage Systems
Location:
Burnaby, BC
Type:
Full-time
Reports to:
Canada R&D Center NPI Manager

Overview

We are seeking an experienced Technical Project Manager to lead the development and industrialization of utility-scale and C&I battery energy storage products. This role owns project execution from concept through mass production. It coordinates mechanical, electrical, firmware, manufacturing, supply chain, and certification teams to deliver products on time, on budget, and to quality targets. The ideal candidate combines strong project leadership with enough hands-on mechanical and electrical depth to engage credibly in design reviews, supplier discussions, and technical trade-off decisions.

Responsibilities

Lead cross-functional BESS product development projects (cabinets, containers, and core subsystems such as BMS, PCS, and EMS) through a stage-gate NPI process, from concept and prototype through validation, pilot build, and mass production.
Build and maintain integrated project plans covering schedule, budget, resources, deliverables, and gate criteria. Track progress and escalate risks early.
Drive technical decision-making across disciplines. Facilitate design reviews and help resolve mechanical, electrical, and thermal integration issues and trade-offs between cost, performance, schedule, and manufacturability.
Own supplier qualification for key components and contract manufacturers. This includes technical evaluation, capability audits, sample and first-article approval (FAI), PPAP/APQP-style deliverables, and ongoing quality performance tracking.
Establish and improve engineering processes, including design review gates, DFMEA/PFMEA, engineering change management (ECR/ECN/ECO), BOM and configuration control, and documentation standards aligned with the company QMS (ISO 9001).
Coordinate certification and compliance activities (UL 9540, UL 9540A, UL 1973, UL 1741, NFPA 855, and related standards) with test labs, engineering teams, and external consultants.
Plan and oversee validation and reliability testing (environmental, thermal, vibration, electrical safety) and track issue closure through production readiness.
Work with manufacturing and supply chain teams on DFM/DFA, line readiness, cost reduction, and supply chain localization in North America.
Serve as the main technical point of contact for internal stakeholders and, where needed, customers and partners. Provide clear status reporting to management.
Coordinate with global R&D and manufacturing teams across time zones.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or higher in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.
3+ years of engineering experience in energy storage, EV, power electronics, or industrial equipment.
Direct experience with utility-scale and/or C&I BESS product development is strongly preferred.
Proven track record taking hardware products from prototype to mass production through a structured NPI process.
Hands-on experience with supplier qualification, supplier audits, and managing contract manufacturers.
Solid working knowledge of both mechanical (enclosures, structures, thermal management, air/liquid cooling) and electrical (HV DC architecture, battery modules and racks, PCS, BMS, wiring and protection) aspects of energy storage systems.
Familiarity with engineering process frameworks such as stage-gate, APQP, DFMEA, and engineering change control. Experience working within an ISO 9001 quality system.
Knowledge of UL/NFPA certification processes for energy storage (UL 9540, UL 9540A, UL 1973, NFPA 855) is an asset.
Proficiency with project management and engineering tools (MS Project or equivalent, Jira, PLM/PDM systems).
Excellent communication, organization, and cross-functional leadership skills, with the ability to drive accountability without direct authority.
PMP or equivalent certification is an asset.
Proficiency in Mandarin is an asset for working with global engineering and supply chain teams.

About PotisEdge

PotisEdge Co., Ltd., founded in 2015, specializes in three core business areas: EV Battery Systems, Smart Energy Storage Systems, and Hydrogen Fuel Battery Systems. With a commitment to "independently developing core BESS technologies across the entire stack," including iCCS, BMS, and EMS, PotisEdge focuses on advancing energy system technologies and delivering innovative smart energy solutions for diverse applications. Join us to lead innovative energy storage projects from concept to market while advancing your career in technical project management.

Job Description:

is looking for an Associate Program Manager

In this role, you'll manage executing assignments for Flexrotor programs and contracts, supporting the development of additional efforts and opportunities to expand our business. You will assist in leading efforts to establish, forecast, implement, and monitor activities associated with the scope, schedule, and budgets of assigned Flexrotor programs/contracts. Concurrently, you'll assist in developing proposals for program enhancements and modifications aimed at increasing revenue. This role requires strong coordination across involved departments; scheduling and budget management; tracking changes; support for contract/proposal execution; and risk assessment and mitigation for assigned programs.

Meet the Team:

The Airbus Helicopters Flexrotor Program offers one of the most advanced small tactical unmanned aerial systems (STUAS) with vertical take-off and landing (VTOL). It can be used day or night by US and allied forces for a diverse range of intelligence, surveillance, target acquisition and reconnaissance (ISTAR) on land and at sea.

Financial Rewards: Competitive base salary, incentive compensation which may include profit sharing schemes, retirement savings plan and the ability to participate in an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (“ESOP”)
Work/Life Balance: Paid time off including personal time, holidays and a generous paid parental leave program.
Health & Welfare: Comprehensive insurance coverage including medical (traditional and high-deductible health plans), prescription, dental, vision, life, disability, Employee Assistance Plan (“EAP”) and other supplemental benefit coverages.
Individual Development: Upskilling and development opportunities through our global Leadership University, including unlimited access to 10,000+ e-learning courses focusing on ways to develop your employability, certifications, career path as well as the opportunity to participate in accelerated development programmes and both national and international mobility.

Your Challenges:

Primary Responsibilities:

Stakeholder Management: (35%)

Work with various cross-functional teams and stakeholders (e.g., Engineering, Business Development, Flight Testing, Flight Operations, Quality, Procurement, Production, Contracts) to bring programs and proposals to completion on schedule, on budget, and on quality.
Ensure all project/proposal team members understand their scope of commitment, are informed of status and next steps, and understand schedule (SPI) and budget (CPI) situations.
Ensure relevant teams are aligned and prepared to implement projects resulting from Flexrotor program initiatives.
Maintain comprehensive documentation for regular reporting at Staff Meetings and Program Reviews.
Act as the primary interface for assigned programs & projects throughout the Flexrotor team and across other organizations when required.

Customer / Partner Management (20%)

Guide customers and partners through the initiation, execution, and close-out processes for assigned Flexrotor program / contract(s).
Focus on customer experience and strict adherence to contractual agreements.
Actively listen, understand, educate, and inform the customer to foster repeat business.
Manage difficult and sensitive situations, ensuring continuous customer satisfaction.

Schedule Management (15%):

Develop and maintain project/program schedules, including predecessors, successors, planned and actual dates for assigned programs.
Make schedule adjustments based on changing project/program and proposal requirements, keeping the project team, customer, and leadership informed.
Responsible for successful on-time / on-budget project/program completion.

Monitor and report on the Schedule Performance Indicator (SPI).

Budget Management (15%):

Verify inputs from functional departments and check overall validity of budget inputs.

Gather costs and track budget expenditures, leveraging technical understanding to identify cost-saving opportunities.
Monitor and report on the Cost Performance Indicator (CPI).

Assist program manager with interpreting contractual requirements for both existing programs and new proposals and solicit feedback from internal counsel as needed.

About the Job

The Senior Project Manager of Infrastructure Project will be part of the core team that will drive the IT Infrastructure strategy and execution of projects in traditional, cloud, and hybrid environments. The individual is responsible for overseeing and driving the successful delivery of complex IT infrastructure projects across the organization. This role provides strategic leadership, governance, and hands-on direction to ensure infrastructure initiatives—covering compute, storage, data centers, networks, cloud platforms, end-user computing, and core infrastructure systems—are delivered on time, within budget, and in alignment with business objectives, security standards, and regulatory requirements.

The role acts as a key interface between technology teams, vendors, PMO, and business stakeholders, ensuring consistent project management practices, risk management, and value realization across the infrastructure portfolio.

Provide leadership, coaching, and direction to project managers and delivery teams, and promote continuous improvement in project delivery practices, tools, and reporting.
Establish and enforce project governance, standards, and methodologies across infrastructure initiatives.
Lead end-to-end delivery of infrastructure projects, from initiation and planning through execution, deployment, and closure.
Manage large-scale and multi-stream projects involving on-premises, hybrid, and cloud infrastructure.
Define project objectives, deliverables, and success criteria aligned with strategic goals.
Work out full-scaled and precise project proposal with technology teams for presentation and approval from senior management.
Ensure projects meet defined scope, quality, timeline, and cost objectives.
Track project milestones and provide clear, timely communication on project status, risks, and decision points to Project Steering Committees and Senior Management.
Ensure compliance with internal policies, PMO processes and standards, security controls, regulatory requirements, and audit expectations.
Manage external vendors, system integrators, and service providers, including contract governance and performance management.
Coordinate and bridge between vendors and internal teams for troubleshooting of issues and post-mortem activities.
Manage project budgets, forecasts, and cost controls.
Optimise resource allocation across internal teams and vendors.
Identify, assess, and mitigate project risks, interdependencies, potential issues proactively, and recommending solutions.
Take accountability in considering business and regulatory compliance risks and takes appropriate steps to mitigate the risks.

We are looking for people with

Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science / IT or Diploma with Professional Certifications.
Professional certification such as PMP, PRINCE2, ITIL, or equivalent is an advantage.
15+ years in leadership experience in IT project management, with significant exposure to infrastructure projects and decision-making capabilities.
Proven experience leading large, complex infrastructure initiatives (e.g. data centre migration, cloud adoption, network refresh, cybersecurity uplift).
Advanced project management skills with strategic planning and program management capabilities.
Demonstrated ability to deliver infrastructure projects at scale with high reliability and minimal business disruption.
Demonstrated experience working with multiple stakeholders at senior management level.
Familiarity with enterprise architecture, service management, and security frameworks.
Strong understanding of IT Infrastructure domains, including datacentres and cloud platforms, network and connectivity, compute and storage, database, disaster recovery / business continuity, etc.
Planning and organizational skills for undertaking team leadership and BAU workload management.
Self-driven with a positive attitude and strong leadership skills to champion for culture change management initiatives within IT and with interfacing Business stakeholders.
Excellent stakeholder engagement, communication, and negotiation skills.
Structured, analytical approach to problem-solving and risk management.
Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, complex environment.
Ability to coordinate complex troubleshooting and post-mortem activities across teams and vendors.

How you succeed

Champion and embody our Core Values in everyday tasks and interactions.
Demonstrate high level of integrity and accountability.
Take initiative to drive improvements and embrace change.
Take accountability of business and regulatory compliance risks, implementing measures to mitigate them effectively.
Keep abreast with industry trends, regulatory compliance, and emerging threats and technologies to understand and highlight potential concerns/ risks to safeguard our company proactively.

new_jobs.description:
Work for Indiana

Begin a fulfilling career with the State of Indiana by joining one of the largest employers in the state, offering a range of opportunities across 60+ agencies. At the state, you'll find competitive compensation, a robust benefits package and a commitment to work-life balance. Most importantly, you'll have the chance to make a real and measurable impact on the lives of Hoosiers across Indiana.

About Indiana Department Of Environmental Management (IDEM)

Our mission is to implement federal and state regulations to protect human health and the environment while allowing the environmentally sound operations of industrial, agricultural, commercial, and governmental activities vital to a prosperous economy. We issue air, water, and solid and hazardous waste permits that restrict discharges to environmentally safe levels. Staff members inspect and monitor regulated entities; provide compliance and technical assistance; monitor and assess air, land, and water quality; use enforcement actions as necessary to ensure compliance; and respond to incidents involving spills to soil or waters of the state.

Role Overview

As a senior project manager within the Petroleum Remediation Section, you will oversee Leaking Underground Storage Tank (LUST) & petroleum/independent closure program sites, guiding petroleum remediation projects from initial incident through final closure. This role involves communicating with internal tech staff, external consultants, liable parties, contractors, attorneys, developers, redevelopment corporations, and owners and operators of regulated storage tanks as necessary. Ensuring responsible parties comply with state and federal cleanup regulations (IC 13-23, IC 13-24, 329 IAC 9, and 40 CFR 280 Subparts E and F). Ensuring liable parties complete the necessary reporting, investigating, and corrective action.

In addition, senior project managers within the section will guide/mentor the junior project managers within the section. Senior project managers also act as subject matter experts for petroleum remediation for internal and external audiences. And they will assist in the management of internal projects.

Key Attributes For Success

Highly motivated and results-driven.
Experienced problem solver & critical thinker.
Demonstrated ability to lead and mentor.

This position requires an Indiana driver's license.

Salary

The salary for this position traditionally starts at $59,800.00 but may be commensurate with education and work experience. Use our Compensation Calculator
to view the total compensation package.

A Day In The Life

The essential functions of this role are as follows:

Interprets laws, regulations and guidelines for assigned environmental program areas.
Develops and modifies existing state programs to adapt to changes in federal or state legislation-mandated policy changes.
Coordinates review of environmental projects and/or program area to meet program needs and objectives.
Maintains a tracking system to ensure that projects are currently working through the appropriate program processes in acceptable timeframes.
Prepares and provides a variety of written communications including responses to letters of inquiry from concerned citizens, elected representatives, government officials, and regulated entities.
Chairs or facilitates a variety of work-related committees as needed.
Utilizes programs and electronic database systems to meet program area needs. Serves as a subject matter expert on applicable systems in program area.
Researches, analyzes, and reports on priority projects and their progress.
May perform audits on environmental programs or facilities and make recommendations for corrective action or improvements.
Provides technical assistance and/or evaluates compliance to environmental regulations and programs.
Coordinates review of requests for variance and exemptions from environmental program regulations
Reviews program plans for completeness, economic and technical feasibility, and environmental impact.
Designs and directs projects regarding specific and complex environmental issues, providing technical expertise for analysis, interpretation, and logistics of projects.
Prepares progress reports for management and senior leadership and provides consultation to management and staff.
Reviews and evaluates technical work reports and supporting data for acceptability and conformance with federal requirements, laws and regulations, conclusions, and recommendations.
Assigns and reviews work of lower-level staff members.

The job profile is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice.

This position is exempt from overtime compensation for additional work hours which may be required to complete essential functions or other assigned work. Exempt employees may work more than 75 hours in a pay period without additional compensation and must report a minimum of 75 hours per pay period of work hours and/or paid leave taken to receive their base biweekly salary.

What You'll Need For Success

Individuals in this role should minimally be able to articulate or demonstrate the following:

Extensive knowledge of theories, practices and principles of Environmental Management and related areas
Thorough knowledge of theories, practices, and principals of physical sciences (chemistry, biology, physics) as they relate to program area
Thorough knowledge of federal and state regulations as they apply to program area and the ability to apply these in a variety of conditions and situations
Ability to conduct surveys, inspections and investigations of facilities and sites, review projects/situations, read plans, interpret ﬁndings, and make recommendations
Ability to establish long- and short-term project management goals and objectives
Ability to prepare documents for administrative and regulatory action
Ability to eﬀectively interact with local, state, and federal groups and government representatives orally and in writing
Ability to prepare accurate and thorough reports
Ability to develop and deﬁne procedures and accomplish objectives within the appropriate and established deadlines
Ability to interpret and implement public policy as it relates to program speciﬁc environmental rules or laws
a Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, Environmental Science, Environmental Policy, Chemistry, Biology, Geology, or a related field with at least 6 years of work experience in an environmental or environmental public health field required.
Related certifications and coursework may be considered for education or experience.

Individuals should have the ability to perform essential functions with or without reasonable accommodation.

Supervisory Responsibilities/Direct Reports

This role may be utilized in a supervisory capacity based on agency needs.

Benefits Of Employment With The State Of Indiana

12 paid holidays, 14 on election years

Free Parking for most positions
Free LinkedIn Learning access

new_jobs.title: Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
About Us

Stimulus Technologies is a leader in technology services, dedicated to bridging the digital divide in underserved communities. With operations across California, Missouri, Nevada, New Mexico, and Oregon, we deliver high-speed, reliable connectivity that transforms lives and businesses. We also offer IT, VoIP, and CyberSecurity services to a range of clients.

Position Overview

Own the project. Navigate the complexity. Deliver on the promise.

As a Project Manager at Stimulus Technologies, you lead grant-funded fiber deployment projects from design kickoff through construction and final network turnover, where execution isn’t just about timelines, but strict compliance, funding milestones, and public accountability. You are the single point of ownership for delivering projects that meet aggressive build schedules while satisfying state and federal grant requirements.

This is a high-ownership role where you’ll manage competing priorities across engineering partners, contractors, internal teams, and clients, while ensuring every decision aligns with budget, schedule, and reimbursement eligibility. You’ll proactively manage risk, enforce accountability, and keep projects moving in an environment where delays and missteps have real financial consequences. If you thrive in complex, high-stakes projects and want to lead work that directly impacts communities, this is your opportunity to take ownership and deliver at scale.

Essential Functions

Project Planning and Schedule Management

Develop and maintain the master project schedule encompassing design, permitting, construction, drop installation, testing, and network turnover milestones.
Coordinate schedule dependencies across the engineering firm (design and permitting), construction contractors (mainline build), and in-house crews (drop installation) to ensure alignment and prevent downstream delays.
Establish project milestones and critical path items; proactively identify schedule risks and develop mitigation plans.
Track and enforce compliance with grant-mandated buildout timelines, reporting deadlines, and program-specific milestone requirements.
Manage project scope and change control processes; evaluate and document the cost, schedule, and scope impact of all change requests before approval.
Facilitate project kickoff meetings and establish roles, responsibilities, and communication cadences with all internal and external stakeholders.

SOW, Contract, and Budget Management

Monitor the engineering firm’s performance against their SOW, deliverable schedules, and contract terms; document deviations and coordinate corrective actions with the Construction Manager and Director of Project Management.
Monitor construction contractor performance against contract terms, pay application accuracy, and change order justifications in coordination with the Construction Manager.
Develop and manage project budgets; track actual costs against forecasts and report variances to the Director of Project Management.
Review and approve invoices from the engineering firm, construction contractors, and permitting agencies for accuracy and contract alignment before processing.
Ensure all project expenditures are properly documented and categorized for grant reimbursement and compliance reporting.
Maintain organized contract files including SOWs, amendments, change orders, and correspondence for each project.

Stakeholder and Client Management

Serve as the primary point of contact for the client on project status, deliverables, and issue resolution.
Prepare and deliver regular project status reports to the client, Director of Project Management, and internal leadership including schedule performance, budget status, risks, and upcoming milestones.
Facilitate regular project status meetings with the client, engineering firm, construction contractors, and internal teams.
Manage client expectations and proactively communicate schedule or scope changes with proposed solutions.
Coordinate with the client on subscriber enrollment, service activation timelines, and drop installation priorities.

Cross-Functional Coordination

Coordinate with the Construction Manager on construction progress, contractor issues, and field resource needs.
Coordinate with the Permitting Manager on permit submittal schedules, approval status, and any permitting constraints affecting the construction schedule.
Coordinate with the Drop Installation Crew Manager on drop scheduling, production rates, and compliance with mandated installation timelines.
Work with the engineering firm to track design and permitting deliverable progress and ensure deliverables feed into the construction schedule on time.
Coordinate the construction-to-operations turnover process, ensuring all documentation, testing, and acceptance criteria are met before network handoff.
Identify resource conflicts or bottlenecks across projects and work with the Director of Project Management to prioritize and resolve.

Grant Compliance and Reporting

Ensure all project activities and documentation comply with state and federal grant program requirements.
Prepare and submit required grant reports, progress updates, and milestone certifications on schedule.
Maintain auditable project records including schedules, budgets, invoices, change orders, and deliverable logs for grant compliance purposes.
Track grant reimbursement submissions and coordinate with finance on draw schedules and funding status.
Stay current on grant program requirements and proactively communicate any compliance risks to the Director of Project Management.

Education and Experience

Required

High school diploma or GED; bachelor’s degree in project management, construction management, engineering, business, or related field preferred.
Minimum 5 years of project management experience in telecom, broadband, fiber optic, or utility construction.
Demonstrated experience managing project budgets, schedules, and contractor/vendor relationships.
Strong understanding of OSP fiber optic construction phases including design, permitting, mainline build, and drop installation.
Experience with SOW and contract compliance management for third-party engineering or construction firms.
Proficiency with project management tools (e.g., Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, or equivalent) and Microsoft Office Suite.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills for client-facing reporting and stakeholder management.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and competing priorities.
Valid driver’s license with the ability to travel to project sites as needed.

Preferred

PMP certification or equivalent project management credential.
Experience with government-funded or grant-funded broadband deployment programs (BEAD, RDOF, ReConnect, CAF, or similar).
Familiarity with FTTH/FTTP deployment at scale.
Background in OSP engineering or construction management.
Experience with grant compliance reporting and reimbursement processes.

Alignment with Core Values

At Stimulus Technologies, our core values define how we work. The ideal candidate will demonstrate:

Driven to Grow – Continuously seeks to develop professionally, stays current with industry practices, and pushes to improve processes and outcomes.
See a Need – Fill a Need – Proactively identifies gaps, obstacles, or opportunities and takes action without waiting to be asked.
Elevate Others – Mentors teammates, shares knowledge freely, and actively contributes to a positive and collaborative work environment.
Extreme Ownership – Takes full accountability for results, decisions, and mistakes; does not deflect blame or make excuses.
Celebrate Success – Recognizes contributions of team members, acknowledges milestones, and fosters a culture where wins are shared.

Management reserves the right to amend and change responsibilities to meet business and organizational needs as necessary.

Introduction

The Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation - Homeowner Protection Program is seeking a motivated and results-driven Administrator III Supervisor to join our team.

This position plays a key role in supporting agency operations by supervising professional and/or support staff, coordinating workflow, implementing policies and procedures, and identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and service delivery. The incumbent may also work closely with executive leadership on special projects, policy development, research, operational planning, and initiatives that support the agency’s overall mission.

The ideal candidate is a confident leader who can effectively manage multiple priorities, communicate clearly, exercise sound judgment, and build collaborative working relationships. We are looking for someone who is organized, adaptable, solutions-oriented, and committed to providing high-quality administrative leadership in a fast-paced public service environment.

If you are ready to bring your leadership, organizational, and problem-solving skills to a position where your work can make a meaningful impact, we encourage you to apply.

GRADE

STD0018

LOCATION OF POSITION

SDAT-Homeowner Protection Program

Tax Sales Ombudsman Department

700 E. Pratt Street, 2nd Floor

Baltimore, Maryland 21202

Main Purpose of Job

The Homeowner Protection Program (HPP) Manager is primarily responsible for running and overseeing the day-to-day operations of the HPP, which removes enrolled homeowners from tax sale by paying off their tax liabilities to Counties or private investors, records a lien on their property, sets them up on a repayment plan, and assists them with paying their debt back to SDAT and planning to pay future taxes that become due.

The Manager ensures efficient and effective management of the Program, which includes application processing, enrollment, payment processing, case management, accounting, and supervising appropriate staff. The Manager continually develops and monitors systems for maintaining quality control, creative troubleshooting, and providing excellent customer service. The Manager continually develops and improves program processes, enrollee assistance strategies, promotional communications, and overall program implementation and evolution when appropriate, both in collaboration with the Ombudsman and independently, to respond to evolving program needs and further program goals.

The HPP Manager is secondarily responsible for assisting the Office of the State Tax Sale Ombudsman. This may include supervising the Tax Sale Specialist, monitoring phone and email inquiries, and by assisting homeowners who are not eligible for the HPP or have not yet become eligible with resolving and avoiding tax delinquency by connecting them with legal services, tax credits, housing and financial counseling, and other helpful resources.

POSITION DUTIES

Manges the Homeowner Protection Program

Oversees and coordinates operations of the Homeowners Protection Program, serving as the Department's subject matter expert on the Program,
Oversees the application process, including an initial review wilhin a reasonable time once an application is received.
Oversees the enrollment process. Reviews all applications fairly and uniformly. To the extent practical, develops objective criteria to evaluate and score applications. Performs final review of applications and recommends enrollees to the TSO.
Oversees handling of enrollees. Manages and tracks accounting aspects of the process. processes loan agreements. manages payments te the counties and private investors. records liens. and tracks monthly payments and status of outstanding debt. Formulates assistance strategies for enrollees, including responsive follow-up when payments are not being made and other communication with enrollees. Takes appropriate action if future tax liabilities become due.
Takes a customer service driven approach, ensuring that the Tax Sale Help line. email, and other points of contact are responded to adequately. Handles customer escalation that otherwise would rise to the level of the TSO.
Sets rules and processes for shared emails, phone queues, and otherwise through use of Freshdesk (email/CRM) and 8x8 (VolP).

new_jobs.description:
About the company

TinkerLabs is a problem-solving and innovation consulancy that applies Design Thinking and Behavioral Science to address complex business and social impact challenges. Since 2013, the team has partnered with 100+ organizations across 15+ industries, including Fortune 500 companies, leading Indian enterprises, and global non-profits. Clients range from Microsoft, Unilever, Tata Group, Mahindra & Mahindra, Flipkart, and L&T to the Gates Foundation, UNFPA, and GIZ. Through consulting engagements, sprints, and workshops, TinkerLabs helps teams generate bold, human-centered, and simple ideas that drive meaningful change. More information about their work and collaborations is available at www.tinkerlabs.in.

About the role

Can you turn ambitious project visions into seamless operational reality? We are hiring for a Program Manager
who can balance high-energy facilitation with rigorous operational mastery for a very important and elaborate education programme at TinkerLabs. 

We’ve partnered with a large corporate to equip students from design and engineering institutes in India to build products and services for a social impact cause using our methodology. The goal is to help students build strong ideas and connect them to an incubator that brings their ideas to life. 

We’re looking for a Program Manager who can run this national-scale design thinking workshop program - you’ll be the force that turns a complex programme run smoothly for all stakeholders involved. And when a session needs a facilitator, you are able to stand up and run it yourself.

This is not a coordination role. You are expected to shape the plan for the year, defend it with the client, and then deliver it.

What will you do

Master multi-city operations:
Build and manage the end-to-end programme roadmap across multiple colleges nationwide. Track milestones, coordinate schedules, mitigate risks and bottlenecks, manage stakeholder and client communications and ensure seamless delivery
Organise the chaos:
Drive key activities and keep track of all moving parts - institutional partnerships, workshop content, facilitators training, workshop sessions, student submissions, feedback loops and important project tasks without missing a beat
Manage client trust:
Lead client-facing communications with poise and empathy. Set clear expectations, navigate bottlenecks seamlessly and bring grounding and ease to complex timelines
Streamline team resourcing:
Balance workloads, forecast talent needs and hire the right people
Manage hybrid delivery:
Seamlessly bridge the gap between digital learning platforms and in-person events across various facilitators- keeping student engagement consistent and the quality of project high
Facilitate with high energy:
Lead engaging, interactive design thinking workshops both in-person and online 

What are we looking for:

Must haves:
Proven facilitation & coaching experience:
3+ years of experience leading workshops, teaching, or facilitating design thinking, human-centered design (HCD), or experiential learning modules.
Genuine facilitation ability:
Has ability to command a room independently for 30+ participants - adapt on the fly when an exercise isn't landing, and build quick rapport with college students and faculty alike
Strong project management chops:
Track record of managing complex projects/programmes with multiple moving parts, stakeholders, and strict deadlines - nothing goes missing when working with you
Solid client management and communication skills
: Comfortable delivering bad news, collaborating on solutions, sending clear emails and being seen as a trustworthy face for the client.
Willingness to travel:
Eagerness to travel to college campuses across India (Tier 1, Tier 2, Tier 3) for live workshop modules

Good to haves:
Experience working with colleges, universities or student communities
in India.
Comfort using AI tools
as part of workshop delivery and content preparation.
A design or education
background.

Besides the work, what is in it for you:

Ownership from day one.
You won't just follow a playbook - you will shape how this massive programme journey unfolds and scales.
High-impact learning.
You will watch students transform from passive learners into confident, empathetic problem-solvers over the course of a full academic year.
High Impact, High Velocity:
We move fast and aim high, offering an environment where you do meaningful, rewarding work while respecting personal boundaries.

How to apply:

To help us get a feel for how you think, we’d love for you to respond to one question:
Tell us about a time when you managed a complex, long-term project with many moving parts. What were the main challenges and how did you pivot from there?

Please feel free to share the response in any format you would do justice to - write it, draw it, record it.

Please share your response, updated resume and relevant work sample/facilitation videos
to curios@tinkerlabs.in
with the subject line: Program Manager_(Your name)

As a human will review all the applications, everyone will receive a reply in due time

Design, build, schedule, monitor, and support ETL pipelines, scripts, and automated data-processing jobs in Azure.

Strong experience with Salesforce reporting, data extraction, integration, and analysis.

Experience with AI-assisted development tools such as Cursor, Claude, GitHub Copilot, or comparable tools.

new_jobs.title: State Youth Ombudsman PROGRAM MANAGER I
new_jobs.description:
Introduction

When you join the Maryland Department of Human Services (DHS), you join a team of more than 5,000 employees across the state dedicated to positively changing the lives of more than 1 million Marylanders each year. We do this by providing economic support, preventive services, and caring for children and adults.

We aim to deliver services so that we more quickly meet the needs of the people we serve. At DHS, we grapple with hard questions to find new ways to foster a culture of bold innovation. We do this to ensure that in Maryland, we leave no one behind.

This is a Management Service position that serves at the pleasure of the Appointing Authority.

GRADE

19

LOCATION OF POSITION

Maryland Department of Human Services

Social Services Administration

25 S Charles St.

Baltimore, MD 21201

Main Purpose of Job

Pursuant to Chapter 158 of the Acts of 2026 (House Bill 980 / Kanaiyah's Law), this high-level professional administrative and legal advocacy position serves as the State Foster Youth Ombudsman for youth experiencing out-of-home care statewide. Housed within the SSA Office of Family Advocacy, the incumbent operates with statutory independence to serve as a neutral, objective advocate for youth, caregivers, guardians, resource parents, and adoptive parents interacting with the Department of Human Services (DHS) and Local Departments of Social Services (LDSS). The primary purpose of this role is to enforce accountability and transparency within the state's child welfare infrastructure. The incumbent independently investigates complex complaints regarding the rights and safety of youth in out-of-home care, resolves systemic and individual service delivery gaps, interprets statutory obligations, and delivers executive-level recommendations directly to SSA and DHS leadership to drive statewide operational and policy improvements. At all times, the incumbent will provide customer service to both internal and external customers that meets or exceeds the standards set by the Department.

POSITION DUTIES

Executes all duties, investigations, and reporting mandates in strict accordance with the statutory requirements of House Bill 980 (Kanaiyah's Law).
Investigates complex, high-profile complaints and alleged violations concerning the rights, placement conditions, and safety of youth experiencing out-of-home care across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions.
Conducts Independent Fact-Finding Reviews to evaluate whether actions taken by LDSS or contractual providers conform to federal and state laws, COMAR regulations, SSA policies, and established child welfare practice standards.
Provides authoritative legal and technical expertise regarding child welfare, juvenile court jurisdiction, out-of-home placement restrictions (including the statutory ban on unlicensed settings), custody/guardianship matters, and due process appeal rights.
Interprets and applies complex legal frameworks, consent decrees, and agency directives to determine appropriate resolutions for aggrieved youth and stakeholders.
Formulates formal corrective recommendations based on investigative findings and consults directly with SSA Executive Leadership, Local Department Directors, and the Office of the Attorney General (OAG) to resolve sensitive or high-risk systemic non-compliance issues.
Ensures absolute statutory compliance with strict confidentiality boundaries, HIPAA, mandated reporting protocols, and disclosure exemptions during all investigative and advocacy operations.
Establishes and leads statewide outreach strategies designed to inform youth in foster care, kinship caregivers, attorneys, and advocacy groups of the Ombudsman’s role, responsibilities, and mechanism for submitting direct complaints.
Engages directly with youth experiencing out-of-home care to ensure their voices, lived experiences, and rights actively inform SSA programmatic improvements and statutory recommendations.
Represents the Office of Family Advocacy on high-level interagency workgroups, legislative committees, and task forces regarding child welfare reform and accountability.
Collaborates with System Partners, including juvenile courts, panel attorneys, the Office of the Child Welfare Ombudsman, and local social work staff to mediate deep-seated disputes and drive positive case-level outcomes.
Directs the Management and Tracking of the statewide Ombudsman case portfolio, ensuring precise, legally secure documentation of all inquiries, case activities, and final resolutions.
Performs advanced data and trend Analysis to identify recurring systemic deficiencies, regional operational patterns, or gaps in service delivery that negatively impact youth stability.
Authors and edits legally mandated annual, quarterly, and ad hoc public reports detailing Ombudsman activities, case statistics, compliance metrics, and actionable policy or statutory recommendations for the Secretary, the Governor, and the General Assembly.

Minimum Qualifications

Education: A Juris Doctor degree or equivalent degree from an accredited school of law.

Experience: Five years of experience as a practicing attorney.

Notes

Candidates for this classification must be members of the Maryland Bar at the time of appointment.
The above requirements are set by Maryland House Bill 980 Guardianship Assistance Program and State Foster Youth Ombudsman – Establishment (Kanaiyah’s Law).
Candidates may substitute U.S. Armed Forces military service experience as a commissioned officer in General Attorney classifications or General Attorney specialty codes in the Legal and Kindred field of work on a year-for-year basis for the required education and experience.

Desired Or Preferred Qualifications

The ideal candidate will possess the following:

One year of experience in representing a government agency, public service law, or serving as an advocate in a community activist/services capacity.
One year of experience in juvenile law, Child Welfare or Human Services.
One year experience as a judicial clerk.
Completion of at least two relevant courses in human services or public policy, OR successful completion of a clinical program or internship in a legal setting serving human services clients.

SELECTION PROCESS

Please make sure that you provide sufficient information on your application to show that you meet the qualifications for this recruitment. We will not consider information submitted after this date. Successful candidates will be placed on the employment (eligible) list. The resulting list may be used for future vacancies with this agency or other state agencies.

If you are in State service and are a promotional candidate, your salary will be determined in accordance with State of Maryland guidelines.

Benefits

As an employee of the State of Maryland, you will have access to outstanding benefits, including: health insurance, dental, and vision plans offered at a low cost. CLICK ON THIS LINK FOR MORE DETAILS: STATE OF MARYLAND BENEFITS .

Personal Leave - new State employees are awarded six (6) personnel days annually (prorated based on start date).
Annual Leave - ten (10) days of accumulated annual leave per year.
Sick Leave - fifteen (15) days of accumulated sick leave per year.
Parental Leave - up to sixty (60) days of paid parental leave upon the birth or adoption of a child.
Holidays - State employees also celebrate at least thirteen (13) holidays per year.
Pension - State employees earn credit towards a retirement pension.
Positions may be eligible for telework.

FURTHER INSTRUCTIONS

The online application process is STRONGLY preferred. If you are unable to apply online, you may mail a paper application and supplemental questionnaire to, Maryland Department of Human Services, Employment Services, Attention: Kendra Young, 25 South Charles St, Room 1116-L, Baltimore, Maryland 21201.

If you have any questions concerning the recruitment process for this position, please email Kendra Young at kendra.young2@maryland.gov; include the job title and recruitment # in the subject line.

If you are having difficulty with your user account or have general questions about the online application system, please contact the MD Department of Budget and Management, Recruitment and Examination Division, at 410-767-4850 or Application.Help@maryland.gov .

TTY Users: call via Maryland Relay.

Provide analytical support through advanced data compilation and predictive modeling for revenue operations, finance, and accounting.
Process EOM reporting package for operational leadership teams.
Generate routine and ad-hoc queries/analysis as requested.
Create SOPs and process flow diagrams as required.
Monitor daily ETL results to ensure source data is loaded in an accurate and timely manner. Troubleshoot and resolve issues, as necessary.

Assist with development and maintenance of data dictionaries, business glossaries, and documentation of data flows/lineage.
Utilize Excel Master Data Services (MDS) and other similar tools to correct mapping errors, remedy duplicates, input missing information, and otherwise ensure consistency and completeness of data related to Payors, Bases/Base Codes, Denial Codes, and the like.
Travel on occasion to revenue cycle operations center in West Plains, MO to interact with management team.

Ability to design and implement discussion-ready, Excel-based dashboards.
Intermediate level of knowledge and experience with sourcing datasets from SQL and a general understanding of data structures and relational schemas.
Basic understanding of Star Schema data model design as it relates to data warehouse and relational database interactions.
Microsoft SQL (SSMS) - Adept knowledge in writing basic to complex T-SQL queries, stored procedures, and views to retrieve data from relational databases or a data warehouse.
Microsoft SQL (SSRS) – Familiarity with MS Visual Studio and knowledge of SSRS package creation, file generation and transmission, and addition of error handlers to assist with troubleshooting.
Databricks – Entry level knowledge of the Databricks Platform/Lakehouse and its integration with Microsoft SQL to facilitate data transfer and data warehousing, and data management.
AI Tools – Entry level knowledge of appropriate, ethical, and responsible usage of AI Tools such as MS Copilot and the like to solve everyday business problems.
Experience in data aggregation, normalization, and data modeling from multiple sources.
Strong quantitative/analytical skills; strong innovation, problem solving, and conceptual thinking abilities.
Ability to solve ambiguous problems and suggest practical ways to solve them.
A working knowledge of the healthcare industry, insurance billing and third-party reimbursement is strongly preferred.

Bachelor’s degree in business, Computer Science, Healthcare Management, or related field from an accredited college or university.
3-5 years of experience working in a business intelligence (BI) related position. Healthcare revenue cycle experience preferred but not required.
Strong experience developing business-friendly decision models that source multiple data sources, formula-based measure creation, and ties aggregations to detailed data.

Proficient with MS Excel, specifically including creation and dynamic use of Pivot Tables and formulaic metrics to analyze data and produce reports.
Entry level knowledge of MS Power BI application and its basic functions.

Research Analyst – Modeling and Meta-Analysis

Reports to Senior Research Consultant Modeling and Meta-Analysis

Job Summary

As a Research Analyst at OPEN Health, you are an essential contributor to our Modeling and Meta-Analysis team, working across various HEOR projects, which may include health economic modelling, indirect treatment comparisons, and trial data analysis. You are proactive, responsive, and able to balance shifting priorities to ensure promises are kept and expectations are exceeded. You will have responsibility for delivering high-quality outputs and ownership of specific project components, deliverables, and timelines. You will support project leads in a fast-paced, multi-disciplinary, international organization. We would love to hear from you if you are a versatile modeler, statistician, or health economist and would like to take the next step in your career.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Designing and constructing health economic models (i.e., cost-effectiveness models, budget impact models) from scratch, as well as adapting existing models
Developing project reports, analysis plans, and other deliverables
Conducting relevant data analyses (i.e., survival analyses, meta-analysis) to support model development
Helping to ensure timely delivery of project subcomponents by proactively flagging changes to scope and timelines to senior colleagues
Supporting with client interactions and outreach to ensure client satisfaction
Assisting with requests for proposals and developing strong client relationships to win new business
Keeping abreast with the latest developments in the field

Experience, Skills, And Qualifications

Master’s Degree or PhD in any relevant science, such as health economics, econometrics, economics, pharmacy, epidemiology, statistics or medical sciences
Experience within the field of HEOR would be an advantage, specifically hands-on experience in the development of cost-effectiveness and budget impact models, and familiarity with the context of health economic modelling, reimbursement dossiers, and health technology assessment submissions
Intellectual curiosity and independence, to include the ability to self-start and self-teach
Experience with (statistical) software: VBA, R (version control, RMarkdown and Shiny), STAN (or equivalent MCMC simulation software) would be an advantage
Full proficiency in MS Office programs: Excel, Word, PowerPoint
Excellent communication skills (both written and verbal) along with the ability to clearly communicate complex methods to other team members and our clients
Proactive, responsive and able to balance shifting priorities
Team player, but also able to work independently
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail
